extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, labor leaders, and readers interested in labor legislation and industrial disputes
extracted.subtask_short: reporting on labor legislation and strikes
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing President Truman's proposed labor bill (fact-finding boards, cooling-off periods, strike controls), the bill text/sections, and reactions from unions and industry. Focus is on statute-like criteria for certifying disputes and the powers/procedures of fact-finding boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of disputes by Secretary of Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Secretary of Labor finds (1) that there is a labor dispute in which the agencies of the government charged with the functions of mediation and conciliation have been unable to bring the parties to agreement, and (2) that a stoppage of work seriously affecting the national public interest and affecting interstate or foreign commerce, or the national defense, or commerce within the District of Columbia or any territory or possession, has resulted or threatens to result from such dispute, the Secretary shall certify such findings to the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such certification of the Secretary shall be published in 'The Federal Register' and shall designate the employer or employers involved, the groups or units of employees involved, and the representative or representatives of such employees. When a question arises concerning representation, the Secretary may request the National Labor Relations Board to certify the names of the representatives and such board shall determine the names in the manner provided in Section 9 of the National Labor Relations Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and designation upon certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon certification by the Secretary, the certification shall be published in The Federal Register and shall designate the employer(s), the employee groups/units involved, and the representative(s) of such employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The employers, employees and representatives so designated shall, for the purposes of this act, be regarded as the parties to the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential appointment window for fact-finding boards
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time within five days after the date of such certification by the Secretary of Labor, the President, in his discretion, may appoint a board to investigate such labor dispute and to make a report containing its findings of fact and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President's appointment is discretionary but limited to the five-day window after certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding board composition and neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Such board shall be composed of three or more persons, none of whom has any pecuniary or other private interest in the employers or employees who are parties to the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership must be neutral with no financial or private stake in the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to records during deliberations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-finding bodies would have access to the records during their deliberations and for at least five days afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards may examine relevant records while investigating and for a limited post-deliberation period to support their findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board investigatory powers and hearing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The board shall proceed expeditiously to make a thorough investigation of all facts which it deems relevant, and shall give the parties a full and fair hearing, which shall include the opportunity to present evidence in support of their claims and to present their case in person, by counsel, or by their representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fairness is required: parties may be represented and present evidence; the board must investigate thoroughly and expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of National Labor Relations Act investigatory powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Section 9 of the National Labor Relations Act (relating to the investigatory powers of the National Labor Relations Board) shall be applicable with respect to any board appointed under this section, and its members and agents, and with respect to the exercise of their functions, in the same manner that such provisions are applicable with respect to the National Labor Relations Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards and their agents have the investigatory powers similar to the NLRB as provided under NLRA sections referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report submission timeline and possible extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Within twenty days after the date of its appointment, the board shall submit to the President a report containing its findings of fact and such recommendations concerning the dispute as the board deems appropriate. The time for submitting the report may be extended by agreement of the parties, or their representatives, with the approval of the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default deadline is 20 days; any extension must be agreed by parties and approved by the President and any agreement shall be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiting/cooling-off period requiring continuation or resumption of work
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of five days following the date on which the Secretary of Labor makes a certification to the President under Section 2, and, if a board is appointed under Section 3, during the period beginning when such board is appointed and ending five days after the date on which it submits its report, the parties to such dispute shall continue or resume work and operations under the terms and conditions of employment which were in effect immediately prior to the beginning of such dispute, except that such terms and conditions may be changed by agreement between the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mandatory short 'cooling-off' window surrounds certification and the board process during which strikes or lockouts must cease and prior terms govern unless mutually changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coercion, instigation, funding or encouragement of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be unlawful for any person to coerce, instigate, induce, conspire with, or encourage any person to interfere with or prevent such work or operations by giving direction or guidance, or by providing funds for the conduct or direction thereof or for the payment of strike or other benefits to those participating therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the covered period aggressive fomenting, funding, or organizational direction intended to interrupt work is explicitly forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of individual employee consent and non-compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this act shall be construed to require an individual employee to render labor or service without his consent, nor shall anything in this act be construed to make the quitting of his labor or service by an individual employee an illegal act; nor shall any court issue any process to compel the performance by an individual employee of such labor or service, without his consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute preserves individual worker freedom: no forced labor and quitting is not criminalized; courts cannot compel individual employees to work against their will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for disputes subject to the Railway Labor Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this act shall be applicable with respect to any labor dispute subject to the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Railway labor disputes remain governed by the separate Railway Labor Act and are excluded from this statute's procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations authorized to carry out the act
rubrics_metrics.description: Such appropriations as may be necessary for carrying out the provisions of this act are hereby authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congressional funding is authorized to implement the bill's provisions; practical implementation depends on appropriations.
